notes: rl2:prerequisiteDuty → odrl:duty on the permission; the duty is also an independent rl2:clause, so it is also an odrl:obligation of the policy, and both roles share one instance. The duty names its own assignee ex:Alice, so it inherits no roles from the permission (architecture §4 item 4) and only evidence with actor ex:Alice is a witness (due2-workflows.md §5.3). Without Alice's preparation, due2 reports Pending with Alice's duty outstanding and Alice as its bearer (workflows §6.3) — the standing Pending/NotApplicable divergence (README). The obligation is in force only when the policy's permission matches the request, so for Alice's own request (scenario 3) it is not reported, whereas RL2 reports the status of every concrete duty in the universe. The text's two side remarks become scenarios 2 and 3; the decision they imply under RL2 is recorded. Scenario 4 is added.
